text: The bazaar awoke with two stalls shuttered overnight: Elsa, the Scribe, and Batman, the Coppersmith, both Villagers. The roster still lists Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Inigo, and Sherlock—no new departures, no new roles revealed. The night’s arithmetic is unchanged since the Herald’s report. Nothing more to weigh.

Hermione, you said "Batman (The Coppersmith) — Villager, by village vote," yet the graveyard names him Villager by vote and Elsa Villager by stall shutter. One of those is a misquote—please correct which entry you meant.

Sherlock, you pressed clause 5 yesterday and today demand "more than silence"; point to the clause text you still seek answered—else your own call is unmet.

Ripley, your silence on clause 5's wording is the same silence you accuse others of keeping.

The bazaar's arithmetic does not change with hopes; it changes when a merchant answers the clause they invoked.

Gandalf, your morning question pressed clause 5 yesterday and today you write the bazaar’s arithmetic does not change with hopes. Which plain fact in the roster or the Herald contradicts your own earlier correct citation?

The bazaar’s arithmetic is the graveyard’s text, Gandalf: Batman is named Villager there, plain in the record. Your insistence that arithmetic outranks that text ignores the Compact’s exact words.

Hermione, you asked which merchant on the roster has not yet spoken today—yet your own voice has not answered that question since. Name the merchant you pressed others to name.

Ripley, silence on clause 5 is the same silence you accuse others of keeping. The bazaar’s Compact is short; its words are exact. Point to the clause text you still seek answered—or say plainly what you meant.
If Sherlock is honest, Sherlock's vote tonight will follow Sherlock's ledger — watch whether it does.

Hermione, you asked which merchant on the roster has not yet spoken today, then counted eight names and seven voices. You named all eight merchants—Gandalf, Yoda, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, yourself, Sherlock, and me—and still your own stall stands silent in the square. The ledger shows eight posts since the morning bell: Gandalf, Yoda, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Sherlock, myself in the morning, and myself again when pressing the graveyard’s text. Gandalf, you pressed the roster arithmetic, yet the roster names you among those who have spoken today. The arithmetic is plain: Hermione, your stall has yet to post.

Sherlock, your clause 5 demand still lacks the clause text you cite; the Compact states plainly: "at most one brief metaphor per statement." Quote the words or drop the accusation—no village will answer silence.

Gandalf, you called the bazaar's arithmetic "yours to correct or abandon," yet your own count omits one post you made. The roster names you among those who spoke today; match the math to the ledger you cite.

Hermione, your own stall has posted zero times today while you pressed others to name a silent merchant—correct your roster claim or withdraw it. The bazaar remembers who counts and who does not.

Ripley, the bazaar’s Compact does not reward silence when you demand exact words from others. You pressed Sherlock and me nine times to quote clause 5 yet never quoted it yourself—your silence is the same standard you applied to us. Sherlock, if clause 5 is your measure, quote the words or withdraw the accusation. Gandalf, your arithmetic now matches the roster’s eight posts; the graveyard names Batman Villager, plain in the record. Hermione, your stall has posted zero times today while you asked others to name a silent merchant; correct your roster claim or withdraw it. The village keeps count.

Sherlock, you asked nine times for clause 5 quoted yet never quoted it yourself—stop demanding what you will not show. Ripley, your silence on clause 5’s wording matches the silence you condemn.

Gandalf, the graveyard names Batman Villager, plain text, yet you called arithmetic yours to correct or abandon. Match the record to the roster or drop the claim.

Hermione, you pressed others to name the silent merchant while your stall has yet to post today—correct your roster claim or withdraw it.

Yoda, Ripley, Morpheus, Neo: you all leaned toward banishing revealed Villagers. The Family still walks unseen among us.

I lean toward banishing Hermione—she pressed others to name the silent merchant while her own stall stands empty, and she has yet to post today.
